expectations.text: States that API clients / API tokens issued by VCF SSO are a 9.1 feature and are NOT available in 9.0
expectations.evidence: '**The feature you're describing ... is new in VCF 9.1. It does not exist in VCF 9.0.**' with the 'Starting with VCF 9.1' doc quote.

expectations.text: Does NOT walk the user through the 9.1 Fleet Management > Identity & Access > API Clients flow as if it existed in 9.0
expectations.evidence: The 'Manage > Fleet Management > Identity & Access > VCF SSO Overview > ... > API Clients' walkthrough is confined to the section headed '## What you get if/when you go to 9.1', and the answer states 'There is no supported way to backport the 9.1 API client feature into 9.0.'

expectations.text: Gives the actual 9.0 route: per-product credentials (SDDC Manager /v1/tokens, VCF Operations token/acquire, NSX session, vCenter session)
expectations.evidence: Per-product 9.0 route given: SDDC Manager `POST /v1/tokens` + refresh/revoke, VCF Operations `POST /suite-api/api/auth/token/acquire` with `Authorization: OpsToken`, vCenter `POST /api/session`. NSX is covered by principal-identity certificate auth rather than the session-create flow, which is the one named mechanism it does not give.

expectations.text: Mentions NSX principal identities as the documented service-account mechanism for NSX
expectations.evidence: 'use a **Principal Identity** with **certificate-based auth** and the **Auditor** (read-only) role.'

expectations.text: Notes that VCF built-in roles (VCF Viewer / VCF Administrator) are documented only in the 9.1 doc set
expectations.evidence: The VCF built-in role names are never mentioned. The 9.1 section describes 'scope + role + validity' generically; VCF Viewer / VCF Administrator / SDDC Viewer / SDDC Administrator do not appear anywhere in the answer.

notes: without_skill states 'SDDC Manager - Still present in 9.0, but **deprecated** - Broadcom has said it will be removed in a future release'. Per vcf-core-9.0.md/vcf-core-9.1-and-deltas.md, the deprecation statement is scoped to the SDDC Manager *UI*; the appliance, service and API are not deprecated, and the 9.1 API grew 375 -> 423 with zero removals. The advice that follows ('Don't build new long-term automation against it') rests on that error.

without_skill gives SDDC Manager roles as 'ADMIN / OPERATOR / VIEWER'; no source in the research corpus publishes SDDC Manager role strings (the with_skill arm explicitly refuses to name them and points at GET /v1/roles).

without_skill's VCF Automation service-account section (device_authorization flow, urn:vcloud:role: scopes, RFC 6749 rotation) is not covered by the research corpus either way - unverifiable from available sources.
